governing_question: What physical and service systems must Arkansas be able to produce, maintain, access, and afford for households and communities to prosper—and how should those systems connect to ownership, markets, public investment and external income?
central_proposition: Arkansas does not have eight independent infrastructures. Productive systems are an interdependent portfolio evaluated by one Productive Systems Test—connecting capacity, ownership, markets, household effects, public roles, external income and resilience—without converting essential services into ideological ownership assumptions or inventing COUNTABLE cash.
organizing_sentence: Pass 3.6 is a systems-integration pass: Food, Energy, Housing, Healthcare, Transportation, Water, Digital and Care under one twelve-dimension test, a Dependency Matrix, a Production Balance Sheet, and ownership/public-role decision architecture from Passes 3.4–3.5.
hard_boundary: 3.6 is a systems-integration pass, not eight independent policy research projects. Do not reopen the food-hub cash-flow hunt. Do not choose a perfect generation mix. Do not write a 300-page healthcare reform. Baseline sufficient to establish the system.

prior_first_pass.note: No dedicated Stage 2 productive-systems engine; harvest Arkansas NOW productive-asset gaps, Money Engine external-income binds, Household housing/care joins, and closed food-hub discipline.

productive_systems_test.title: Productive Systems Test
productive_systems_test.rule: Every productive system gets evaluated through the same twelve-dimension framework.

FOOD.label: Food & Agriculture

test.NEED: Nutrition, food security, farm livelihoods, institutional feeding
test.DEPENDENCY: Inputs, processing capacity, some retail/wholesale chains
test.CAPACITY: Land, producers, partial processing — facility CF unproven for public income
test.OWNERSHIP: Spectrum: household farms → private → cooperatives → external → public claims only after waterfall
test.MARKET: Competitive access varies; concentration risk at processing/retail
test.MONEY_FLOW: Margin accumulates often outside farm gate — Extraction Test applies
test.PUBLIC_ROLE: Rulemaker/referee primary; investor/owner only if Role Conflict Test clears
test.TRANSITION: Processing access + ownership pathways — not invent COUNTABLE now

principles: Food security + farmer prosperity + processing capacity + market access + local retention + external sales + resilience
Large agricultural production ≠ proven processing margin ≠ public cash
Facility validation remains an implementation gate
FOOD.not: Do not reopen the food-hub cash-flow hunt.

ENERGY.label: Energy

test.NEED: Power for households, industry, care, digital, food processing
test.CAPACITY: Generation, T&D, industrial demand — detailed inventory OPEN
test.OWNERSHIP: Utilities / coops / IPPs / public — Role Conflict Test if public owns
test.MONEY_FLOW: Household/business bills → utilities/fuel → possible export surplus
test.PUBLIC_ROLE: Rulemaker/referee heavy; provider/investor only if justified
test.TRANSITION: Reliability + affordability + eventual export — sequenced in 3.7/Stage 4

principles: Not merely cheaper electricity — competitive productive system that can generate external income
Connect household economics with Money Engine
Do not choose a perfect future generation mix here
ENERGY.not: Generation-mix optimization belongs to deeper sector testing.

HOUSING.label: Housing & Land

test.CAPACITY: Stock/supply geography OPEN; AV FACT proxy
test.MARKET: Ownership vs rental; local concentration varies
test.HOUSEHOLD_EFFECT: Cost, security, ownership, time (commute join transport)
test.EXTERNAL_INCOME: Limited — industry wages; not primary export thesis

principles: Housing is simultaneously shelter, a market good, a household expense, a productive industry and—for many households—a primary wealth asset
Policy that treats only one dimension can damage another
Connect Pass 3.2 household burden to production
HOUSING.not: Do not resolve property-tax rates here — Dependency Rule + 3.4 taxonomy.

HEALTHCARE.label: Healthcare

test.NEED: Health capability enabling work, care, longevity
test.MONEY_FLOW: Household/public → payers → providers → often external capital

principles: Healthcare spending is not itself prosperity. Health capability is.
Distinguish increasing capacity/outcomes from simply increasing expenditures

TRANSPORTATION.label: Transportation & Logistics

test.NEED: Work, school, healthcare, food, civic participation + farm→export logistics
test.MARKET: Competitive freight; household transit thin in rural areas
test.PUBLIC_ROLE: Provider of infrastructure; referee of safety; limited transit provider

principles: Two interconnected systems: household mobility and productive logistics
TRANSPORTATION.not: Not a full statewide transportation master plan.

WATER.label: Water & Natural Systems

test.DEPENDENCY: Climate, upstream systems, chemicals/energy for treatment
test.OWNERSHIP: Public utilities, districts, private wells, stewardship regimes
test.PUBLIC_ROLE: Strong provider/rulemaker for drinking water & wastewater

principles: Water is household necessity + agricultural input + industrial input + infrastructure + natural capital
WATER.not: We don't need a statewide water plan in 3.6 — political-economic architecture only.

DIGITAL.label: Digital Infrastructure

test.NEED: Participation in modern economy and civic life
test.OWNERSHIP: Private ISPs, coops, public options possible
test.PUBLIC_ROLE: Rulemaker/referee; possible investor for last-mile gaps
test.TRANSITION: Coverage + competition — not AI compact reopen

principles: Broadband determines access to work, education, healthcare, markets, finance, government, AI capability, entrepreneurship
Distinguish infrastructure from data-rights/governance closed in Pass 3.5

CARE.label: Care Infrastructure

test.NEED: Enable labor participation + dignity for dependents
test.MONEY_FLOW: Household/public → providers; unpaid care is invisible subsidy
test.HOUSEHOLD_EFFECT: Time, cost, security — direct HP join
test.PUBLIC_ROLE: Rulemaker + often payer/provider of last resort
test.TRANSITION: Treat as economic infrastructure in 3.7 sequencing

principles: Childcare, disability support, aging/long-term care determine whether other household members can participate economically
CARE.not: Do not dissolve care into healthcare-only.

dependency_matrix.title: Productive Systems Dependency Matrix
dependency_matrix.purpose: Reveal single points of systemic weakness. Not every relationship needs quantitative weights yet. Invaluable for Stage 4 resilience testing.
dependency_matrix.note: Energy, transportation, water and digital appear repeatedly as cross-cutting dependencies.

ownership_decision_architecture.title: Essential systems versus public ownership
ownership_decision_architecture.principle: An essential service does not automatically imply government ownership.
applies: Pass 3.5 Four Roles + Role Conflict Test
questions: Can competitive private markets provide it effectively?
Does public ownership improve or impair competition?
Could regulation achieve the objective instead?
ownership_decision_architecture.rule: Functional analysis rather than ideological ownership assumptions.

integration_spine.title: Physical economy inside Constitutional Capitalism
integration_spine.while: Government protects competitive markets (3.4–3.5) and COUNTABLE stays $0 until reserved public cash clears.

counterarguments.strong_form: Comparative advantage says import everything cheaper.
counterarguments.architecture_answer: Productive retention ≠ autarky (3.4). Production Balance Sheet weighs capacity, dependency, resilience and household effect—not slogans. Some local capacity is insurance; some is waste—Stage 4 distinguishes.
Register exposures now; stress-test in Stage 4. When does redundancy become waste is an explicit Stage 4 question.

counterarguments.claim: Public investment crowds out private capital.
counterarguments.strong_form: Any public productive role kills markets.
counterarguments.architecture_answer: Ownership decision tree + Role Conflict Test + Four Roles. Essential ≠ public ownership. Regulation may suffice.

counterarguments.claim: Arkansas should specialize, not seek broader capacity.
counterarguments.architecture_answer: External income CURRENT where demonstrated; Dependency Matrix targets single points of weakness—not autarky. Specialize where markets work; harden where fragility destroys households.

counterarguments.claim: Government cannot identify productive opportunities competently.
counterarguments.architecture_answer: COUNTABLE firewall forbids claiming public income without reserved cash. Public roles prefer rulemaker/referee; investor/owner only after Conflict Test. Facility validation is an implementation gate.

counterarguments.claim: Reducing external dependency sacrifices comparative advantage.
counterarguments.architecture_answer: 3.4 productive retention: happily send money out when exchange produces greater value. Balance Sheet tracks both dependency and external sales.
Comprehensible Government + Public Dollar Chain + Capture Loop breakers (3.5). Appropriation ≠ outcome.

counterarguments.claim: Expanding housing supply undermines existing household wealth.
counterarguments.architecture_answer: Housing's multi-dimension principle: shelter + wealth + industry. One-dimension policy can damage another—Balance Sheet forces joint view; Stage 4 models incidence.

counterarguments.strong_form: Export ambitions raise local prices or cut reliability.
counterarguments.architecture_answer: Architecture lists affordability, reliability and export as co-constraints—not a chosen mix. Sequencing is 3.7/Stage 4.

counterarguments.claim: Rural healthcare capacity can never be economically efficient.
counterarguments.strong_form: Close rural hospitals; concentrate in metros.
counterarguments.architecture_answer: Health capability ≠ spend. Access/time/security are household prosperity dimensions. Efficiency definitions that erase access fail the Productive Systems Test.
Explicit Stage 4 attack vector. Dependency Matrix + resilience exposures create the test bed; 3.6 does not pretends to settle it.

certification.statement: Pass 3.6 completes Arkansas Productive Systems as systems integration: Productive Systems Test; eight systems; Dependency Matrix; ownership decision architecture; Production Balance Sheet; external-income classifications; resilience exposures; Arkansas evidence; counterarguments; seven visuals. Food-hub cash-flow not reopened. COUNTABLE +$0. No sector rabbit holes.
